worthless

/WURTH-lis/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Worthless means having no real value or importance.

At the antiques fair, a jeweler examined the gleaming watch and gently declared the counterfeit worthless.

Example

Rosa finally cleaned out the kitchen drawer and tossed a thick stack of coupons — every one had expired months ago, making them worthless at the register.

The coupons once had value, but past their expiration dates they cannot save a single cent. With no value or usefulness left, they are exactly what worthless describes.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

valueless: Valueless states as a neutral fact that something has no monetary or practical value — the shares became valueless. Worthless says the same thing with a curl of the lip: worthless junk, a worthless guarantee. Appraisers call a fake valueless; its furious owner calls it worthless.

useless: Useless means failing to serve a purpose — it measures a thing against a job. A key that opens nothing is useless. Worthless measures against value: what the thing would fetch or deserve. A flat spare tire is useless today but not worthless; a counterfeit bill is both.

pointless: Pointless means having no purpose or benefit, and it attaches to actions and efforts — a pointless meeting, a pointless argument. Worthless attaches to things and their value: worthless coupons, a worthless fake. Searching a worthless mine is pointless; the mine itself is worthless.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

valuable: worth a great deal

priceless: so valuable no price can be put on it

Where it sits · how little good it brings

cheap → worthless → harmful

cheap vs. worthless: A cheap souvenir still has a little value; a worthless one has none at all.

harmful vs. worthless: Harmful goes a step beyond worthless — a worthless gadget merely wastes drawer space, while a harmful one actively causes damage.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — worth: value (Old English weorth)

Suffix — -less: without (Old English -leas)

Put it together: Worth + -less literally builds "without value" — this word wears its meaning right on its sleeve.

Use the root in a new word: noteworthy: The intern's noteworthy idea ended up saving the company an entire week of work.

Root Check

Word Choice

Neutral / everyday

Use worthless for things that have lost or never had value: worthless junk, a worthless guarantee, a worthless fake. Be careful applying it to people — calling someone worthless is harsh and hurtful, and careful writing reserves the word for objects, documents, and efforts.
